label: Declassified

szenen.text: The U.S. *secretly* read Soviet spy messages for decades.
It began in *1943* and ran until 1980.
Soviet cables were meant to be *unbreakable.*
But code clerks *reused* keys. That was the crack.
Decrypts helped *expose* spies inside the atomic program.
The public learned of it only in *1995.*
A secret kept for *50 years.* Who is reading your messages today?

caption: Venona ran from 1943 to 1980 and stayed secret until 1995. Who do you think is listening today? Send this to someone who doesn't believe it. AI voice & edit. Footage: Pixabay/Pexels.
